title: A Claude delegation in explorer mode with writePolicy readOnly is not read-only: its tools are auto-approved and it can stage and write files
outcome: Every delegation that TermAl accepts with writePolicy readOnly is enforced as read-only by the host, whatever its mode. A Claude child spawned in explorer mode with readOnly is either answered by the host read-only classifier (ReadOnlyAutoApprove with its permission overlay), or the spawn is refused with a typed error that names the supported mode. It never runs with tool approval it was not given.
acceptance: A Claude delegation spawned in explorer mode with writePolicy readOnly runs under ClaudeApprovalMode::ReadOnlyAutoApprove: its spawn arguments carry the read-only overlay (--settings with permissions.ask ["*"], sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed false, disableAllHooks true), and the host read-only classifier answers its tool requests. A deterministic test shows that configure_delegation_child_prompt_settings gives a Claude explorer+readOnly child ReadOnlyAutoApprove, and that its Bash `git add .` and `node -e …` requests are refused while `git status --short` is admitted.

A test enumerates every (agent, mode) combination that delegation creation accepts with writePolicy readOnly. It asserts that each child is configured with an enforced read-only setting (Claude ReadOnlyAutoApprove, a Codex read-only sandbox with approval never, Cursor or Gemini Plan, Kimi Ask in default mode, or the agent's equivalent), or that the spawn is refused with a typed error before any child starts. No accepted readOnly combination runs with auto-approval.
docs/features/agent-delegation-sessions.md states that writePolicy readOnly is host-enforced for every accepted agent and mode, including Claude explorers, and names any combination that is refused.
Focused verification and the maintained gate pass on the final input.
